name: Shuangbaotai Animal Manure Management System GHG Mitigation Project in Guangdong Province
description:
Shuangbaotai Animal Manure Management System GHG Mitigation Project in Guangdong province introduces new animal waste management systems to a group of 9 swine farms in Guangdong Province, which are owned by Shuangbaotai Animal Husbandry Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter called” Shuangbaotai”). Each subsidiary swine farm will install one animal waste management system, and the manure is treated on site. The purpose of the project activity is to treat the manure and wastewater to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons.

The project activity uses flushing system to collect the manure automatically. All the manure and wastewater are collected and then be separated first. The separated solid will be treated in aerobic composting system to produce fertilizer and the fertilizer will be distributed to the surrounding farmers free of charge to improve the life condition of farmers. The separated liquid will be treated through anaerobic digestion, the biogas generated during the treatment process will be captured for power generation and the Residual biogas (if any) will be flared. The power generated will only be used by the 9 swine farms. The sludge produced from anaerobic digestion will be treated through aerobic composting together with the solid and the effluent will be used as a liquid organic fertilizer for the irrigation of agriculture.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals
methodology: ACM0010 GHG emission reductions from manure management systems
project_developer: Profit Carbon Environmental Energy Technology (Shanghai) Co., Ltd.

name: Swine Farm Animal Manure Management System GHG Mitigation Project in Hubei Province
description:
Swine Farm Animal Manure Management System GHG Mitigation Project in Hubei Province introduces new animal waste management systems to a group of 9 swine farms in Hubei Province, which are owned by Jiangxi Zhengbang Breeding Co. Ltd (hereinafter called” Zhengbang”). The purpose of the project activity is to treat the manure and wastewater from the 9 swine farms to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons.
The project activity will replace the current open anaerobic lagoons with 9 new closed anaerobic digesters. The biogas generated during the treatment process will be captured for power generation, the electricity generated are all used by the swine farms. After anaerobic digestion, the fermented sludge will be treated in aerobic composting system, which will be used as fertilizer. Wastewater from the new animal waste management systems will be treated aerobically and then used for agriculture irrigation

name: Circle Gas LPG Smart Meter Program in Kenya
description:
The proposed project activity (Circle Gas LPG Smart Meter Programme in Kenya) has been developed by Circle Gas to reduce reliance on wood, charcoal, and kerosene used for cooking by households in target areas. This will be achieved through distribution and installation of LPG units fitted with smart meters to track usage. The project adopts a Pay as You Go (PAYG) approach to accelerate access to LPG and contribute to sustainable development goals.
a) The project entails distribution and installation of PAYG LPG units made distinct by the smart meter developed by Circle Gas.
b) The project developer is Circle Gas, with formal responsibility for the activity.
c) The VPA implementor is M-Gas Kenya, responsible for maintaining the sales database, collecting baseline data, and coordinating annual monitoring.
d) The project is a voluntary action by the developer.
e) The goal is to accelerate LPG access among low-income households, reducing GHG emissions and negative effects of traditional fuels.
The project replaces biomass and kerosene cookstoves with LPG units, delivering impacts across multiple areas:
• Health: LPG reduces dirty fuel use, improving indoor air quality and lowering respiratory illness risks, especially for women and children. HAP causes ~21,560 deaths annually in Kenya (SDG 3).
• Climate: LPG emits low black carbon and PM2.5, meeting WHO guidelines and reducing climate impacts (SDG 13).
• Gender: LPG eliminates fuel collection, saving time for women and girls, enabling education and income activities (SDG 4 & 5).
• Savings: LPG reduces fuel costs for low-income urban families and creates jobs (SDG 1).
• Energy Access: Affordable cooking energy is provided (SDG 7).
• Jobs: Employment is created, especially for youth in sales, service, and management (SDG 8).
The project boundary is Kenya. Carbon rights are transferred to Circle Gas via waiver signed at installation.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals
poa_project_name: Circle Gas LPG Smart Meter Program

name: Circle Gas LPG Smart Meter Program
description:
The proposed programme (Circle Gas LPG Smart Meter Programme) has been developed by Circle Gas to reduce reliance on wood, charcoal, and kerosene commonly used for cooking in households and commercial facilities like restaurants within target areas. This will be achieved through distribution and installation of LPG units connected to a smart meter to track and monitor LPG usage by end-users. The programme adopts a Pay as You Go (PAYG) approach to accelerate access to LPG. The PoA also aims to contribute towards sustainable development goals. The specific description of the PoA is as follows:
a) The PoA entails distribution and installation of PAYG LPG units made distinct by the unique smart meter developed by Circle Gas.
b) The project developer will have formal responsibility for the PoA and will be directly responsible for maintaining sales records, collecting baseline information, and annual monitoring.
c) The PoA is a voluntary action by the project developer.
d) The goal is to increase access to LPG, especially among low-income households, significantly reducing GHG emissions and other negative effects associated with the use of traditional fuels.
The PoA aims to replace biomass and kerosene cookstoves with LPG units, delivering impacts across multiple areas:
• Health: LPG replaces dirty fuels, improving indoor air quality and reducing respiratory illnesses, especially for women and children (SDG 3).
• Climate: Biomass and kerosene stoves emit GHGs. LPG cuts CO₂ and black carbon, helping mitigate climate change (SDG 13).
• Gender: Biomass stoves require frequent fuel collection, mostly by women and girls. LPG saves time, enabling income-generating activities and supporting education (SDG 4 & 5).
• Savings: Fuel scarcity drives up prices, straining budgets. Circle Gas targets low-income urban communities, offering savings and creating jobs (SDG 1).
• Energy Access: Affordable cooking energy will be achieved through this programme (SDG 7).
• Jobs: The project will create employment, especially for youth in field sales, service, and management (SDG 8).
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals

name: Beam Mobility Micromobility
description:
Beam Mobility Holdings Pte Ltd (The Company) is in the business of operating and managing e Mobility and e Vehicle rentals, including e Scooters, in Australia, New Zealand, and other countries in the Asia Pacific region, operating under relevant laws, regulations and licensing arrangements.

Based on an independently prepared and verified Life Cycle Assessment for Beam’s operations in Wellington and Auckland, involving the deployment of 1,200 e Scooters, Beam is confident in its assertion that this will result in material and meaningful carbon emission reductions over the lifetime of the operating tenure, as compared to a baseline emissions footprint of alternative modes of transport, specifically including Internal Combustion Engines (ICE), Public Transport, Electric Passenger Vehicles.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals
methodology: AMS-III.BM: Lightweight two and three wheeled personal transportation version 1.0

name: Congo (DRC) Improved Cook Stoves VPA 003– Ngaliema
description: The goal of the proposed VPA is to distribute improved cookstoves (“ICS”) in the neighborhoods of Ngaliema, a commune of Kinshasa. Vitol SA is the coordinating/managing entity (CME) of the VPA.The project ICS combust biomass fuels more efficiently, reducing the greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and Particulate Matter (PM) emissions, thus improving the indoor air quality in project households. Due to the higher thermal efficiency of the ICS relative to the traditional/baseline stoves, the ICS reduce the amount of non-renewable biomass fuel required for meeting similar thermal energy needs. Thus, replacement of the baseline inefficient stoves with project ICS will reduce non-renewable biomass fuel consumption and hence generate emisison reductions.
